scenes.tts: The first film followed a gold, GTP-loaded switch until cutting turned it slate. If cutting ends that interval, what happens when something blocks the cut or speeds it up? Use the same colors and the same switch.
scenes.caption: The first film followed a gold, GTP-loaded switch until cutting turned it slate. If cutting ends that interval, what happens when something blocks the cut or speeds it up? Use the same colors and the same switch.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's COLOR MAP exactly: GDP/off = slate; GTP/on = gold; GEF action = teal; GAP action = clay-red. Restore its membrane, one large gold GTPase, three-tab GTP token, and growing schematic activity trace. Split the off arrow into blocked and accelerated branches.
scenes.narration: The first film followed a gold, GTP-loaded switch until cutting turned it slate. If cutting ends that interval, what happens when something blocks the cut or speeds it up? Use the same colors and the same switch.

scenes.visual: Brief title over the carried moving world: How the Timer Breaks. The gold block pulses and its schematic trace continues growing.

scenes.tts: Begin with the ordinary cycle. A teal loading event starts a gold interval. Intrinsic cutting later removes the final phosphate, leaving GDP and ending the interval. This is our neutral reference for every perturbation.
scenes.caption: Begin with the ordinary cycle. A teal loading event starts a gold interval. Intrinsic cutting later removes the final phosphate, leaving GDP and ending the interval. This is our neutral reference for every perturbation.
scenes.visual: Run one full schematic cycle in the same positions as the first film. Teal GTP loading turns the block gold; a moving time bar extends; the third phosphate tab detaches; the block turns slate. Keep a neutral baseline trace above and label it 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Begin with the ordinary cycle. A teal loading event starts a gold interval. Intrinsic cutting later removes the final phosphate, leaving GDP and ending the interval. This is our neutral reference for every perturbation.

scenes.tts: Replace GTP with an analogue the protein can bind but cannot cut. Loading still turns the switch on. Nothing changes at the loading arrow. The off event fails, so the gold interval persists after receptor input ends.
scenes.caption: Replace GTP with an analogue the protein can bind but cannot cut. Loading still turns the switch on. Nothing changes at the loading arrow. The off event fails, so the gold interval persists after receptor input ends.
scenes.visual: Transform the normal three-tab token into an uncuttable labelled block without molecular structure. A cutting blade icon reaches the last tab but cannot detach it. The receptor dims while the gold block and schematic trace continue; label the trace 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Replace GTP with an analogue the protein can bind but cannot cut. Loading still turns the switch on. Nothing changes at the loading arrow. The off event fails, so the gold interval persists after receptor input ends.

scenes.tts: Cholera toxin reaches the same logic through Gs. Its modification obstructs Gs alpha's hydrolysis, so adenylyl cyclase remains active and cyclic AMP stays elevated. The timer stalls downstream of the receptor.
scenes.caption: Cholera toxin reaches the same logic through Gs. Its modification obstructs Gs alpha's hydrolysis, so adenylyl cyclase remains active and cyclic AMP stays elevated. The timer stalls downstream of the receptor.
scenes.visual: Reset to a normal gold Gs-alpha block beside an adenylyl-cyclase dial. A toxin marker adds a small obstruction badge to Gs, never a structure. The phosphate tab stays attached, the dial remains ON, and cyclic-AMP dots continue rising under a 'schematic' label.
scenes.narration: Cholera toxin reaches the same logic through Gs. Its modification obstructs Gs alpha's hydrolysis, so adenylyl cyclase remains active and cyclic AMP stays elevated. The timer stalls downstream of the receptor.

scenes.tts: Now add extra RGS protein to an already-loaded G alpha that this RGS can regulate. All other parts begin matched. Should its active interval grow longer, grow shorter, or stay unchanged?
scenes.caption: Now add extra RGS protein to an already-loaded G alpha that this RGS can regulate. All other parts begin matched. Should its active interval grow longer, grow shorter, or stay unchanged?
scenes.visual: Clear the toxin badge and return the trace to neutral. A clay-red RGS block approaches a gold susceptible G-alpha block. Place three equal choices above the growing schematic interval: longer, shorter, unchanged.
scenes.narration: Now add extra RGS protein to an already-loaded G alpha that this RGS can regulate. All other parts begin matched. Should its active interval grow longer, grow shorter, or stay unchanged?

scenes.visual: Hold all three choices without highlighting one. The gold interval continues creeping right and the RGS block hovers nearby. Keep subtle membrane drift as the only motion.

scenes.tts: Shorter. RGS accelerates cutting for the Gi and Gq families. The final phosphate leaves sooner, so the block returns to slate earlier. That family boundary matters. RGS does not have this effect on Gs.
scenes.caption: Shorter. RGS accelerates cutting for the Gi and Gq families. The final phosphate leaves sooner, so the block returns to slate earlier. That family boundary matters. RGS does not have this effect on Gs.
scenes.visual: Highlight 'shorter'. The clay-red RGS produces fast chevrons along the off arrow; the phosphate tab detaches and the block turns slate. Then place a small Gs block beside the path with a neutral 'not this RGS target' label, not a universal prohibition.
scenes.narration: Shorter. RGS accelerates cutting for the Gi and Gq families. The final phosphate leaves sooner, so the block returns to slate earlier. That family boundary matters. RGS does not have this effect on Gs.

scenes.tts: Ras G twelve V breaks GAP-assisted cutting differently. GAP may bind, but the catalytic arrangement fails. This is catalytic failure, not missing GAP. Ras therefore remains GTP-bound far longer than normal.
scenes.caption: Ras G12V breaks GAP-assisted cutting differently. GAP may bind, but the catalytic arrangement fails. This is catalytic failure, not missing GAP. Ras therefore remains GTP-bound far longer than normal.
scenes.visual: Transform G alpha into a single membrane-tethered Ras block labelled 'Ras G12V'. A clay-red GAP docks at the same outer position, but the internal schematic cutting alignment stays offset. Do not draw atoms. Extend the gold trace and label it 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Ras G12V breaks GAP-assisted cutting differently. GAP may bind, but the catalytic arrangement fails. This is catalytic failure, not missing GAP. Ras therefore remains GTP-bound far longer than normal.

scenes.tts: Ras Q sixty-one, shown beside it, also weakens cutting, even without GAP. Both mutants keep the gold interval abnormally long. They damage the off route, although their detailed defects differ.
scenes.caption: Ras Q61, shown beside it, also weakens cutting, even without GAP. Both mutants keep the gold interval abnormally long. They damage the off route, although their detailed defects differ.
scenes.visual: Add a second Ras block labelled 'Ras Q61' beside G12V. Remove GAP from the Q61 row, keep both gold traces prolonged, and show two differently shaped misalignment icons. Label both mechanisms 'schematic'; do not merge them into one cause.
scenes.narration: Ras Q61, shown beside it, also weakens cutting, even without GAP. Both mutants keep the gold interval abnormally long. They damage the off route, although their detailed defects differ.

scenes.tts: Dominant-negative Ras S seventeen N is the mirror image. It binds GTP poorly and fails to activate targets. That failure sits on the loading side. It may also hold exchange factors away from normal Ras.
scenes.caption: Dominant-negative Ras S17N is the mirror image. It binds GTP poorly and fails to activate targets. That failure sits on the loading side. It may also hold exchange factors away from normal Ras.
scenes.visual: Reset both prolonged traces. Show a slate Ras block labelled 'Ras S17N'. A gold GTP token approaches but rarely settles, while a teal SOS block remains held beside mutant Ras. Use a dotted arrow and the word 'may' for SOS sequestration.
scenes.narration: Dominant-negative Ras S17N is the mirror image. It binds GTP poorly and fails to activate targets. That failure sits on the loading side. It may also hold exchange factors away from normal Ras.

scenes.tts: Sort every case by its changed arrow. The analogue, toxin, and activating Ras mutants obstruct cutting. Extra RGS accelerates cutting only for its substrates. Dominant-negative Ras impairs loading. One cycle can therefore organize every case.
scenes.caption: Sort every case by its changed arrow. The analogue, toxin, and activating Ras mutants obstruct cutting. Extra RGS accelerates cutting only for its substrates. Dominant-negative Ras impairs loading. One cycle can therefore organize every case.
scenes.visual: Build one large cycle, not a list of disconnected chips. Move the analogue, toxin, and Ras-mutant labels onto the cutting arrow; move RGS onto fast chevrons along that arrow; move S17N onto the teal loading arrow. Keep all labels at least 28 pixels.
scenes.narration: Sort every case by its changed arrow. The analogue, toxin, and activating Ras mutants obstruct cutting. Extra RGS accelerates cutting only for its substrates. Dominant-negative Ras impairs loading. One cycle can therefore organize every case.

scenes.tts: This classification predicts direction, not the exact shape of every cell response. Receptor shutoff, target kinetics, and messenger clearance still contribute. The map keeps that limit visible. First locate the changed step, then judge the trace.
scenes.caption: This classification predicts direction, not the exact shape of every cell response. Receptor shutoff, target kinetics, and messenger clearance still contribute. The map keeps that limit visible. First locate the changed step, then judge the trace.
scenes.visual: Zoom out to show receptor, GTPase, target, and fading messenger dots in one pathway. Highlight only the altered arrow in turn while the other processes remain visible at lower contrast. Never cross out or reject them.
scenes.narration: This classification predicts direction, not the exact shape of every cell response. Receptor shutoff, target kinetics, and messenger clearance still contribute. The map keeps that limit visible. First locate the changed step, then judge the trace.

scenes.tts: A lasting signal is therefore not mysterious once the cycle is mapped. Ask whether loading increased, cutting slowed, or clearance changed. The same map prevents blaming the receptor automatically. The position of the defect determines the prediction.
scenes.caption: A lasting signal is therefore not mysterious once the cycle is mapped. Ask whether loading increased, cutting slowed, or clearance changed. The same map prevents blaming the receptor automatically. The position of the defect determines the prediction.
scenes.visual: The pathway compresses into three moving controls labelled loading, cutting, and clearance. The cutting control enlarges for this film, while the others remain visible. A gold interval stretches when cutting slows and contracts when cutting speeds.
scenes.narration: A lasting signal is therefore not mysterious once the cycle is mapped. Ask whether loading increased, cutting slowed, or clearance changed. The same map prevents blaming the receptor automatically. The position of the defect determines the prediction.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only, large and centered: 'Block GTP cutting to prolong signaling; speed it to shorten signaling.' No title, subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
